record.title: Anthropic’s preliminary S-1 reports rapid growth alongside compute financing exposure
record.summary: Anthropic’s October 26, 2026 preliminary Form S-1 reports $11.6 billion in revenue and $1.0 billion in operating income for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $787 million in revenue and a $1.2 billion operating loss in the same 2025 quarter. The filing says consumption-based services made up 80% of first-half 2026 revenue and 48% of revenue came through cloud-provider marketplaces. It reports $112.4 billion in cash and $19.3 billion in short-term investments at June 30, 2026; the six-month 2026 figures are unaudited. The filing also describes multi-year minimum-purchase and take-or-pay compute obligations, a shift toward leased accelerators and dedicated facilities, and conditional infrastructure financing. The filing describes capacity up to $42 billion under a Broadcom arrangement for 2026 lease obligations, up to $30 billion from Google (none issued by June 30, 2026), and up to $20 billion from Amazon; separately, it reports $10.2 billion aggregate principal of notes issued to two accredited investors by the filing date. These facility ceilings do not establish cash drawn, amounts paid or compute delivered. Several aggregate compute-commitment totals are left blank in the preliminary filing. Large reported net losses include non-cash fair-value remeasurement of convertible notes and related instruments. These disclosures describe the company’s reported results and financing structure; they do not establish compute utilization, future revenue, total realized compute cost or a completed IPO.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Anthropic filed a preliminary Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on October 26, 2026, proposing an initial public offering whose share count and price were left incomplete in the reviewed filing.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The filing reports $11.6 billion in revenue and $1.0 billion in operating income for the three months ended June 30, 2026, versus $787 million in revenue and a $1.2 billion operating loss in the same 2025 quarter; it reports $112.4 billion in cash and $19.3 billion in short-term investments as of June 30, 2026. The six-month 2026 financial figures are unaudited.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The filing says consumption-based revenue represented 80% of total revenue for the six months ended June 30, 2026, and customer sales through cloud-provider marketplaces represented 48% of total revenue in that period.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic describes long-term compute agreements with minimum-purchase or take-or-pay obligations, a move toward leased accelerators in dedicated facilities, and conditional partner financing facilities. It reports capacity of up to $42 billion under a Broadcom arrangement for 2026 lease obligations, up to $30 billion from Google (none issued by June 30, 2026), and up to $20 billion from Amazon; separately, it reports $10.2 billion aggregate principal of notes issued to two accredited investors by the filing date. Maximum facility amounts are not the same as amounts issued, drawn, paid or converted into operational capacity.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reviewed preliminary filing does not establish aggregate compute commitments in the blanked summary fields, delivered or utilized compute by supplier, total realized compute cost, future revenue durability, or completion of the proposed IPO.

evidence_gaps.description: The preliminary prospectus leaves aggregate compute purchase and lease commitment totals and schedules blank in reviewed passages.
Conditional note-purchase and equity facilities are not reconciled here to actual issuance, drawdown, conversion, debt maturity or payment obligations.
The filing provides no supplier-level compute delivered/used, utilization, workload economics or matched unit-cost comparisons.
The registration and proposed IPO were not complete in the reviewed preliminary filing.

brief.importance_rationale: If sustained, the reported scale of usage revenue, financing and long-term compute obligations could materially affect infrastructure procurement and frontier-model economics. A score of 6 reflects substantial implications for one major lab while preserving that the filing is company-specific, several 2026 figures are unaudited, and delivered capacity, commitment totals and future returns remain unresolved.
limitations: The S-1 is preliminary; the proposed share count and offering price are blank, and the registration had not become effective in the reviewed filing.
Six-month 2026 financial figures are unaudited; results are issuer disclosures.
The filing attributes much of the reported net loss to non-cash fair-value remeasurement of convertible notes, derivative liabilities and SAFEs; net loss must not be treated as operating cash burn.
The filing describes conditional partner facilities and up to amounts that are not equivalent to actual issuance, cash draw, spending or delivered compute.
Aggregate long-term compute commitment and payment amounts are blank in reviewed preliminary passages.
Cloud-provider marketplace revenue share is not the same as compute-provider share or compute utilization.
No evidence reviewed establishes future revenue persistence, total return on compute investment, or the final offering outcome.

relationships.summary: SpaceX separately reported a compute-services contract with Anthropic. The S-1 reviewed here does not allocate compute utilization or spending to SpaceX, so the two disclosures are related context rather than a supplier-share reconciliation.

technical.claimed_result: The company reports Q2 2026 revenue of $11.6 billion, operating income of $1.0 billion, and cash plus short-term investments of $131.7 billion at June 30, 2026. It reports 80% of first-half 2026 revenue was usage-based and 48% flowed through cloud-provider marketplaces.
technical.compute_or_cost: The filing describes substantial multi-year compute commitments, leased infrastructure and conditional facilities. It reports up to $42 billion of Broadcom financing capacity for 2026 lease obligations, up to $30 billion from Google (none issued by June 30, 2026), up to $20 billion from Amazon, and $10.2 billion aggregate principal of notes issued to two accredited investors by filing date. These maxima and issued notes are different measures; the reviewed preliminary passages leave aggregate compute commitments blank and establish no supplier-level utilization, realized unit cost or total compute spend.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preliminary S-1 was filed and its disclosed text is publicly inspectable. The filing itself establishes the issuer’s reported statements, not future performance or realized compute delivery.
technical.mechanism: Not a technical model result. The filing describes the company’s commercial and infrastructure model: usage-metered API/application revenue, cloud-provider marketplace distribution, multi-year compute procurement, and increasing use of direct accelerator leases in dedicated facilities.
technical.regime: Anthropic, PBC issuer disclosures in a preliminary Form S-1 filed October 26, 2026. Revenue and balance-sheet amounts cover periods through June 30, 2026, except customer and some compute disclosures dated September 30, 2026.
technical.reproducibility: The SEC filing is publicly accessible. Company financial metrics are disclosed, not independently reconstructed in this activation. FY2025 statements are audited by EY; six-month 2026 statements are unaudited.
technical.strongest_baseline: The filing compares the June 2026 quarter with the same quarter in 2025 and reports audited FY2025 financial statements; six-month 2026 data are unaudited.

brief.title: Anthropic’s preliminary S-1 reports rapid growth alongside compute financing exposure
brief.why_it_matters: The filing gives a rare, detailed view of how one frontier AI company links model demand, usage-based sales, cloud distribution, long-dated compute commitments and capital access. If sustained, those relationships could materially shape compute procurement and the economics of frontier model development. The numbers are issuer disclosures, much of the 2026 period is unaudited, aggregate commitment totals are unavailable in the reviewed preliminary text, and no compute-utilization or future-return result follows from them.

other.title: SpaceX discloses a $1.25B monthly Anthropic compute agreement with a 90-day exit right
other.summary: SpaceX's May 20, 2026 SEC Form S-1 says it entered cloud-services agreements with Anthropic for compute access across Colossus and Colossus II. SpaceX states that Anthropic agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month through May 2029 after discounted ramp-up fees in May and June 2026, while either party may terminate on 90 days' notice. A June 1 SEC response repeats the stated monthly amount and says SpaceX did not view the contracts as a substantial dependence because capacity and revenue could be redeployed. The filing establishes the issuer's disclosed contract terms, not realized payments, delivered capacity, utilization or a guaranteed three-year spend.
